entries.name: if-rule-1001-degraded-spend-reject#0
entries.description: The spent box's tree is the size-flagged v0 tree If(false, Int 1, sigmaProp(true)) (08 07 95 01 00 04 02 08 d3). The JVM builds If without comparing its branch types and types it as its true branch, Int, so rule 1001 degrades the tree at ingest. A spend interprets that UnparsedErgoTree, whose error is not a soft fork, and throws: the transaction is invalid. An impl that parses the tree leniently evaluates it to sigmaProp(true) and accepts. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cand-empty-fiat-shamir-proof-accept#3
entries.description: The spent box's tree is the SigmaProp constant CAND() (00 08 96 00), and the input carries the JVM prover's proof: 24 bytes, the conjecture's Fiat-Shamir challenge over the transaction's message, which needs no secret. The JVM verifies it: valid. An impl that normalizes CAND() to TrueProp, or rejects it at parse, diverges. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cand-empty-no-proof-reject#4
entries.description: The same CAND() box with no proof: CAND() is not TrueProp, so an empty proof fails: invalid. An impl that normalizes CAND() to TrueProp accepts it. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: sigmaand-node-empty-reject#10
entries.description: The spent box's tree is the SigmaAnd node with no items (00 ea 00), which parses. Unlike the CAND() constant (#3), the node is evaluated: SigmaAnd goes through allZK, which calls CAND.normalized (CSigmaDslBuilder.scala:134-136), and that requires a non-empty list (SigmaBoolean.scala:165): the reduction throws before any proof is checked, and the transaction is invalid. An impl that reduces the empty node to TrueProp accepts. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: sigmaand-node-256-true-accept#12
entries.description: The SigmaAnd node of 256 × sigmaProp(true) (00 ea 80 02 08 d3…), which parses (no bound at 255). CAND.normalized skips every TrueProp and returns TrueProp, so the box spends with no proof: valid. An impl that bounds the node's items, or the CAND it builds, at 255 rejects it. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cthreshold-2of3-real-children-accept#13
entries.description: The spent box's tree is the SigmaProp constant CTHRESHOLD(2, [pk1, pk2, pk3]) (00 08 98 02 03 …), i.e. atLeast(2, Coll(pk1, pk2, pk3)), and the input carries a real 2-of-3 threshold proof the JVM prover built from two of the three secrets: valid. The crypto-verification cost is 11993 JitCost = 20 (parse the one coefficient) + 18 (evaluate the degree-1 polynomial at the three children) + 15 (the threshold node) + 3 × 3980 (three ProveDlog leaves); an impl that omits the 15 for the node estimates 11978 and, after the /10 block-cost scale, reports a transaction cost 2 lower (1197 vs 1199). The only transaction vector with a threshold over real children; the degenerate ones (#5, #6, #9) pin n = k = 0 only. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cthreshold-k0-cand-truncated-proof-no-coefficient-accept#14
entries.description: The spent box's tree is CTHRESHOLD(0, [CAND()]) (00 08 98 00 01 96 00): a threshold with one leafless child and no leaves of its own. The input carries a 24-byte proof — the root Fiat-Shamir challenge alone, with no polynomial coefficient. SigSerializer reads the n−k = 1 coefficient with readBytesChecked, which returns the zero bytes that are left and only warns (SigSerializer.scala:156-163, :247-253); GF2_192_Poly takes length / 24 = 0 coefficients, a degree-0 polynomial equal to the root challenge, and the single child's challenge is that same value. A leafless tree's Fiat-Shamir bytes carry no challenge, so the recomputed root challenge matches: valid, where the JVM's own prover writes 48 bytes (the challenge and one coefficient). An impl that reads the coefficients strictly and refuses a short proof rejects it. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cthreshold-k0-cand-truncated-proof-half-coefficient-accept#15
entries.description: The same CTHRESHOLD(0, [CAND()]) box with 12 more proof bytes: the 24-byte root challenge, then half of the 24-byte coefficient. readBytesChecked again returns fewer bytes than requested; GF2_192_Poly takes 12 / 24 = 0 coefficients, so the proof verifies exactly as #14 does: valid. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.

entries.name: cor-empty-fiat-shamir-proof-reject#16
entries.description: COR() (00 08 97 00) with a 24-byte proof equal to its own Fiat-Shamir challenge (hashFn(00 01 00 00 ++ message), the empty-OR node's challenge). The JVM still rejects: parseAndComputeChallenges reads an OR's last child as or.children(nChildren − 1) = children(−1) for the empty OR, which throws, and verifySignature catches every Throwable and returns false (SigSerializer.scala:234, Interpreter.scala:473-481). So COR() is unspendable with any proof, not only the empty one (#7). An impl that reads COR() like CAND() — no children, only the root challenge checked — accepts this proof; #3 (CAND() with the same kind of proof) is its valid twin. The input spends a box of value 1000000000 into one output of the same value; no proof unless noted.
